methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $32M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Gritt is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $32.4M to date. Valuation is undisclosed. The peer universe consists of nine companies: one public entity (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics operating in the same sector and stage band.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, using the $32.4M raised as a proxy for post-money value and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier between Series A and subsequent stages, implies a valuation of $65M. Peer-median analysis draws from four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed)—yielding a median of $1.7B and a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide implied range of $55M to $2.0B, with a median of $882M. This dispersion reflects fundamental stage and scaling uncertainty: stage-progression anchors to near-term fundraising mechanics, while peer multiples embed later-stage capital efficiency and market validation. The peer set skews toward Series B, making direct comparability to an early-stage Series A uncertain. Key risks to valuation include execution risk, competitive positioning within the peer set, and the degree to which peers' valuations reflect durable competitive advantage versus capital availability cycles.
